question: Does a task written as a design conversation (few reads asked for, one-line answers) hold enough context and enough thinking for thinking-cutting to be tested on it: does its context pass the 140k trigger, and how much thinking does it hold by then?
rule: One new task, bug-hunt-six: six real MLflow bugs (fixed upstream in #26171, #26172, #26180, #26130, #26244, #26245) reported one at a time as symptoms over fourteen turns, with short answers asked for, on the commit before the oldest fix. Written 2026-11-17 before any run. One session with no proxy, to size it; not a comparison. The first sizing task, design-tool-choice, peaked at 38k of context with 2.5k of thinking and is not used.
